description:
From the fz-kdt.186 cold review (2026-09-03). driven_backend_program is
called once per fixture per gate (seat gate, twins gate, order-agreement
gate, census gate) and six more times per fixture inside the census gate's
stress loop, so compiler2_dispatch_blind_escape_census_is_the_known_
population alone runs 160-230 s (run-to-run spread +/-40%), the lib suite
went ~100 s -> 221 s at fz-kdt.178's landing (22 fixtures x 7 arrivals), and
the cost of the RELATION under test (one `overlaps` per pair per subject
against ~20 s of compilation) cannot be measured at all. CONCORDANCE: fz-
kdt.175 is the matrix's wall-clock tripwire (a different gate); fz-kdt.141
owns the stress knob these gates drive. Direction: one per-(fixture, arrival)
backend product cache shared by the gates in a test run (the artifact is
immutable once driven), so each fixture compiles once per arrival; then
report the gates' own wall clock as a number. Proportional compilation applies
to the test suite too.
title: The static dispatch gates recompile the same 22 census fixtures per gate and per stress setting: 160-230 s of the 221 s lib run is repeated compilation, and no relation change can be timed
